In this checkout (`/workspace/linux`), there is **no symbol named `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`** and no `intel_display_suspend`; the corresponding current symbols are `intel_runtime_suspend()` and `intel_display_driver_suspend()`.

## PCI PM callback registration

`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c:1025-1031` attaches:

```c
.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops
```

`drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c:1713-1753` defines the callbacks.

## Call chains reaching `i915_drm_suspend()`

The system-suspend callback:

```text
PCI PM .suspend
  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                         [i915_driver.c:1392]
     -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)               [i915_driver.c:1404]
```

The hibernation poweroff callback uses the same callback:

```text
PCI PM .poweroff
  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                         [i915_driver.c:1745]
     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)               [i915_driver.c:1404]
```

The hibernation-freeze callback reaches it directly, without going through `i915_pm_suspend()`:

```text
PCI PM .freeze
  -> i915_pm_freeze(kdev)                          [i915_driver.c:1487]
     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)               [i915_driver.c:1493]
```

Other suspend-related PCI PM callbacks do **not** reach `i915_drm_suspend()`:

```text
.suspend_late
  -> i915_pm_suspend_late()
     -> i915_drm_suspend_late()

.suspend_noirq
  -> i915_pm_suspend_noirq()
     -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq()

.poweroff_late
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_late()
     -> i915_drm_suspend_late(..., true)

.poweroff_noirq
  -> i915_pm_poweroff_noirq()
     -> i915_drm_suspend_noirq(..., true)

.freeze_late
  -> i915_pm_freeze_late()
     -> i915_drm_suspend_late(..., true)
```

Thus, the callbacks that reach `i915_drm_suspend()` are:

- `.suspend` → `i915_pm_suspend()` → `i915_drm_suspend()`
- `.poweroff` → `i915_pm_suspend()` → `i915_drm_suspend()`
- `.freeze` → `i915_pm_freeze()` → `i915_drm_suspend()`

## Callers that also call runtime suspend

None of those callers call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend()`—that symbol does not exist in this tree.

Runtime suspend is a separate PM callback:

```text
PCI PM .runtime_suspend
  -> intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)                   [i915_driver.c:1545]
```

Registered at `i915_driver.c:1752`:

```c
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
```

`intel_runtime_suspend()` performs its own suspend sequence, including:

```text
intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)
  -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)
  -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
  -> intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
  -> intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
  -> intel_uncore_suspend(gt->uncore)
  -> intel_display_power_suspend(display)
```

It does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend()` or `i915_drm_suspend()`.

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The repository has no `intel_display_suspend()` function. The relevant current call is `intel_display_driver_suspend()`.

The data flow is:

```text
device *kdev
  |
  | kdev_to_i915(kdev)
  v
struct drm_i915_private *i915
  |
  | &i915->drm
  v
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
  |
  | to_i915(dev)
  v
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
  |
  | dev_priv->display
  v
struct intel_display *display
  |
  | intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
  v
display suspend implementation
```

Specifically, in `i915_drm_suspend()` (`i915_driver.c:1103-1120`):

```c
struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
...
intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
```

So `dev_priv` is recovered from the DRM device with `to_i915(dev)`, then its `display` member is passed to the display suspend routine.
